title: Frontend: Rick And Morty Characters Viewer
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Rick And Morty Characters Viewer. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App({pages=[[Ada],[Lin]],failPage=-1}). A character-directory exercise uses injected page arrays of names instead of a live external API. Initial page 0 is rendered as li. Next/Previous[data-action=next/previous] await an async adapter, clamp page, show Ready or Unable to load in [data-testid=status]. Failed page clears rows; navigating back recovers. Disable boundary buttons.
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Treat the external API as a replaceable data source with a documented response adapter.
alternativeApproaches: Add a cache with explicit freshness rules and avoid replaying cached data from a different query.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: No matches; fetch failure; out-of-order response.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
